title: microsoft/agent-lightning — The absolute trainer to light up AI agents.
content:
3,500-Line Lightweight Agentic RL Framework for Training Agents with Real Harnesses!
Documentation · Technical Report · WeChat Group (微信群) · MIT License
Agent Lightning was completely refactored in v1.0. For legacy releases earlier than v1.0, see this branch.
- 🪶 ~3,500 lines of code: We treat simplicity as the first principle.
- 🧩 Train with real agent harnesses: Agents interact with the model through the Agent Lightning v1.0 proxy with ZERO changes, while keeping tools, context, control flow, and environments in the loop.
- ☸️ Native Kubernetes support: Run agents directly as Kubernetes Jobs without relying on external sandbox services.
- 💻 Full coding agent training example: Using only 6K training samples, an end-to-end Qwen3.5-9B workflow improves SWE-bench Verified from 41.8% to 56.4%, a gain of 14.6 percentage points. We release the full pipeline, including data cleaning, reward-hacking prevention, and training scripts.
The following is an example installation on a CUDA 13.0 machine:
cd <this-repo>
uv sync
bash scripts/setup_verl.sh 0.8.0 cu130
See the Installation Guide for details.
Agent Lightning v1.0 keeps the training architecture simple with three lightweight components:
- Trainer: Runs verl and vLLM, builds training samples, and updates the policy.
- API Gateway: Proxies model requests and captures training data.
- Rollout Controller: Runs agents locally or as Kubernetes Jobs.
The Trainer creates rollouts, the Controller launches agents, and the Gateway turns interactions into training data, while agents continue to run with their real harnesses.
We evaluate Agent Lightning v1.0 across several practical training domains, including Search R1, LLM-in-Sandbox, and Coding Agent. Pure RL delivers substantial improvements across all three domains, as shown below.
- 8/19/2026 Agent Lightning v1.0: Towards Harnessed Agentic RL technical report.
- 12/17/2025 Adopting the Trajectory Level Aggregation for Faster Training Agent-lightning blog.
- 11/4/2025 Tuning ANY AI agent with Tinker ✕ Agent-lightning Medium. See also Part 2.
- 10/22/2025 No More Retokenization Drift: Returning Token IDs via the OpenAI Compatible API Matters in Agent RL vLLM blog. See also Zhihu writeup.
- 8/11/2025 Training AI Agents to Write and Self-correct SQL with Reinforcement Learning Medium.
- 8/5/2025 Agent Lightning: Train ANY AI Agents with Reinforcement Learning arXiv paper.
- 7/26/2025 We discovered an approach to train any AI agent with RL, with (almost) zero code changes. Reddit.
- 6/6/2025 Agent Lightning - Microsoft Research Project page.
- DeepWerewolf — A case study of agent RL training for the Chinese Werewolf game built with AgentScope and Agent Lightning.
- AgentFlow — A modular multi-agent framework that combines planner, executor, verifier, and generator agents with the Flow-GRPO algorithm to tackle long-horizon, sparse-reward tasks.
- Youtu-Agent — Youtu-Agent lets you build and train your agent with ease. Built with a modified branch of Agent Lightning, Youtu-Agent has verified up to 128 GPUs RL training on maths/code and search capabilities with steady convergence. Also check the recipe and their blog Stop Wrestling with Your Agent RL: How Youtu-Agent Achieved Stable, 128-GPU Scaling Without Breaking a Sweat.

report.summary: Microsoft's Agent Lightning v1.0 is a 3,500-line open-source RL framework that trains real AI agents with zero harness changes, boosting a 9B coding agent 14.6 points on SWE-bench Verified.
report.background: Reinforcement learning for LLM agents has been split between two worlds: researchers who train models on synthetic, stripped-down tasks, and developers who ship agents wrapped in complex harnesses — tool APIs, memory, multi-turn control flow, sandboxes. Bridging them usually meant rewriting the agent, losing context, and drifting tokenization. Microsoft Research's Agent Lightning, first published in August 2025, proposed training any agent with (almost) zero code changes. Version 1.0, released under MIT license with a 2026 technical report, is a full rewrite around that idea: a proxy intercepts model calls so the agent keeps its real tools, prompts, and environment while training data is captured silently. The timing matters because agentic RL is becoming the dominant post-training workload, yet tooling remains fragmented and heavyweight.
key_points: Zero-change training via proxy: Agents keep their existing tools, context, control flow, and environments. An API Gateway sits between the agent and the model, capturing every interaction as training data — no refactoring, no retokenization drift, no rewriting the harness for RL.

Three lightweight components: A Trainer (running verl and vLLM) builds samples and updates the policy; an API Gateway proxies requests; a Rollout Controller launches agents either locally or as native Kubernetes Jobs — removing the need for external sandbox services.

Small codebase, big claims: Roughly 3,500 lines of code, with simplicity framed as the first design principle. The release includes installation scripts, data cleaning, reward-hacking prevention, and full training pipelines rather than a research demo.

Strong empirical results: Using only 6,000 training samples, an end-to-end Qwen3.5-9B workflow lifts SWE-bench Verified from 41.8% to 56.4% — a 14.6 percentage point gain — with substantial gains also reported on Search R1 and LLM-in-Sandbox tasks.

Growing ecosystem adoption: External projects already build on it, including AgentScope's DeepWerewolf case study, AgentFlow with Flow-GRPO, Youtu-Agent (verified up to 128-GPU RL training with stable convergence), and Tinker-based tuning integrations.
report.impact: For the AI industry, this lowers the barrier to agentic RL dramatically: if training requires no harness rewrite, teams can fine-tune the agents they already ship rather than maintaining a separate research stack. That could push agent improvement from hand-crafted prompt engineering toward continuous, data-driven loops. For developers, the practical appeal is cheap: uv sync, a setup script, and existing agent code keeps working while a proxy collects trajectories — plus native Kubernetes jobs mean scaling without bespoke sandbox infrastructure. For regular users, the near-term effect is better coding and search agents from smaller, cheaper models — a 9B model nearing 56% on SWE-bench Verified suggests frontier-adjacent agent performance without frontier-scale serving costs. The risk is standard: easier RL means more automated reward hacking, which the release explicitly tries to guard against.
report.tools: Watch the Agent Lightning repo and its technical report (arXiv 2608.17528) first. Underneath, the stack is verl for RL orchestration and vLLM for fast inference. Adjacent projects worth trying: AgentScope for multi-agent harnesses, AgentFlow (Flow-GRPO for long-horizon sparse-reward tasks), Youtu-Agent (proven 128-GPU scaling recipes), and Thinking Machines' Tinker for tuning agents without heavy infrastructure.
